name: One-Pan Sloppy Joe Casserole

ingredients.buy: 1/2 cup plus 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
9 bell peppers, diced (about half red, half green)

writer_notes: All 15 locked buy lines are used by a step; no orphaned ingredients and no step uses an unbought item.

Source method calls for olive oil, melted butter (brushed on biscuits), and parsley garnish; none are in the buy list, so they were deliberately left out of the steps and added to forbidden_prose_terms.
Turkey is seared in the dry hot pan since no cooking oil is bought; the turkey's own fat carries the aromatics.
Biscuits: three 8-count cans yield 24, recipe uses 21 (halved then peeled into thinner rounds).
cost_ps rendered as the {{cost_ps}} token; no per-line costs used and no package arithmetic claims made (no cost_lines in dispatch).
766 cal sits near the top of the 450-800 band; flag if the engine retightens.

prose.intro_html:
Sloppy joes are one of the great cheap dinners of all time, but the sandwich version has a flaw: the bun goes to mush and you are eating over the sink by bite three. This casserole fixes that. Same sweet and tangy turkey filling, except the biscuits go on top and bake up golden, so the bread holds its ground instead of surrendering to the sauce.

We build the whole thing in one oven-safe pan and scale it to 14 servings, which is the part that matters when you are cooking for the week. Ground turkey keeps it lean, the sauce does the heavy lifting on flavor, and a lid of cheese and biscuit makes every container feel like a real dinner instead of a punishment. At 766 calories and {{protein}} g of protein per serving, this eats like comfort food and budgets like a spreadsheet.
prose.shop_smart:
The biscuits are the one place people overthink this. You want three 8-count cans of refrigerated biscuits, the big flaky kind, and you halve each one through the middle so it bakes thin and crisp instead of doughy. Three cans give you 24, you use 21, and the spares are a fine breakfast the next morning.

For the turkey, buy it in the largest pack you can find rather than the little trays. You need 4 2/3 pounds and the family pack always comes out ahead of the one-pound units. Ground beef swaps in one for one if it is on sale that week and the macros still land in range.

Shredded cheddar is your call between a bag and a block you grate yourself. Either way you need about 4 2/3 cups, which is roughly a pound and change. The sauce is all pantry staples you likely already own: tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire, tomato paste, and the dry seasonings. Buy the no salt added tomato sauce if you can find it so you stay in control of the salt.
prose.make_it:
Heat your oven to 375 degrees. In a bowl, whisk together the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. That is your sloppy joe sauce. Set it aside.

Get a large oven-safe skillet hot over medium-high. Add the minced garlic and stir it for about a minute until it smells good. Add the diced yellow onion and the tomato paste and cook a minute or two, letting the paste darken a shade. Toss in the diced bell peppers and cook another 3 to 5 minutes until everything softens.

Push the vegetables to one side and add the ground turkey. Let it sear undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes before you start breaking it into pieces. Cook it all the way through, until it hits 165 degrees inside and there is no pink left.

Drop the heat to medium-low and pour in the sauce. Stir to bring it together and let it simmer 5 to 6 minutes so it thickens up. Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top.

Peel each halved biscuit apart at the center to make two thinner rounds and lay them across the top of the filling. Slide the pan into the oven and bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the biscuits are golden brown and cooked through.
prose.portion_html:
This one bakes as a single big pan, so portioning is a weigh-and-divide job. Once it comes out and settles for a few minutes, set your empty container on the scale, zero it out, and split the whole batch across 14 containers as evenly as the numbers let you. Aim to give each container a fair share of filling and a biscuit or two on top so nobody opens a sad lid of plain meat.

The biscuits crisp up in the oven and hold better than a bun ever would, which means these reheat honestly. Fourteen servings at {{protein}} grams of protein each is a full week of lunches or dinners that actually keep you full.
prose.cost_closing_html: This is meal prep doing exactly what it is supposed to do: a comfort-food dinner, built lean, split 14 ways so the cost per serving stays down at {{cost_ps}}. That is the whole pitch. You are not choosing between eating well and spending little, you are getting both in the same container.
prose.upsell_html: If this is the kind of math you like on your dinner, the whole Thrifty Crew library runs on it, and membership is a dollar a month. Cook once, eat all week, and let the numbers work for you instead of against you.

head.description: One-pan sloppy joe casserole for meal prep: lean ground turkey in a sweet-tangy sauce under cheddar and golden biscuits, scaled to 14 high-protein servings.
head.keywords: sloppy joe casserole, meal prep, ground turkey, high protein dinner, budget meal prep, one pan dinner, biscuit casserole, batch cooking
steps: Heat the oven to 375 degrees. Whisk together the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire, onion powder, black pepper, and salt to make the sauce, and set it aside.

In a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat, cook the minced garlic about a minute, then add the diced onion and tomato paste and cook another minute or two until the paste darkens. Add the diced bell peppers and cook 3 to 5 minutes until softened.
Push the vegetables aside and add the ground turkey. Sear 2 to 3 minutes, then break it up and cook until browned and 165 degrees inside.
Lower the heat to medium-low, pour in the sauce, stir to combine, and simmer 5 to 6 minutes until it thickens.
Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the top. Peel each halved biscuit into two thinner rounds and arrange them over the filling.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until the biscuits are golden brown and cooked through, then portion across 14 containers.
